# Count of Smaller Numbers After Self

## Problem

You are given an integer array `nums`. Build and return an array `counts` of the same length. For every position `i`, `counts[i]` is how many elements located after index `i` (that is, at indices `j > i`) have a value strictly less than `nums[i]`.

Input format: the first line contains the length `n`. The second line contains the `n` values of `nums`, separated by spaces.

```text
n
nums[0] nums[1]... nums[n-1]
```

Output format: print the `n` entries of `counts` on one line, separated by spaces.

```text
counts[0] counts[1]... counts[n-1]
```

Example 1:

```text
Input:
4
5 2 6 1

Output:
2 1 1 0
```

Explanation: To the right of `5` are `2` and `1`, both smaller, giving `2`. To the right of `2` only `1` is smaller, giving `1`. To the right of `6` only `1` is smaller, giving `1`. Nothing lies to the right of `1`, giving `0`.

Constraints:

* $$1 \le n \le 100{,}000$$
* $$-10{,}000 \le \text{nums}[i] \le 10{,}000$$
* For each index, count only the elements on its right whose values are strictly smaller than it.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

For each index you only care about elements to its right, so think about processing the array from right to left while remembering what you have seen.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a Fenwick tree or segment tree over compressed values, or a merge sort that counts inversions while tracking original indices.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

A naive double loop is O(n^2), aim for O(n log n) and handle duplicates carefully since the comparison is strictly less.

</details>
